clue.text: Occur daily, early

parts.note: to occur is to be, to exist or take place
The Times is a daily newspaper

explanation.surface: Something that happens every day, and early in the day at that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'daily' is not an adverb here but a noun: a daily paper, namely The Times.
explanation.definitionFit: Betimes is an old word meaning in good time or at an early hour.

clue.text: Call for peace to take the wind out of one's sails

definitions.text: to take the wind out of one's sails

explanation.surface: Someone appeals for quiet in order to deflate a rival.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Be calm!' is a plea for quiet; to becalm a ship is to leave it with no breeze to move it.

clue.text: Fruitful result of having to include financial backer

indicators.note: include means the backer's word is put inside the other

parts.note: taken as written
an angel is a theatrical backer who puts money into a show

explanation.surface: A productive outcome came from bringing in a sponsor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fruitful result' is the definition: a tangelo is a fruit bred from tangerine and pomelo.
explanation.definitionFit: The tangelo is a citrus hybrid, literally the product of crossing two fruits.

clue.text: National hero upset America about nothing very awful

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the horse's name is turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: Red Rum was the racehorse that won the Grand National three times
O is the zero figure for nothing

explanation.surface: A national hero overturned American interests over nothing at all terrible.
explanation.walkthrough: The Grand National is Britain's great steeplechase; Red Rum is its most famous winner. 'upset' turns REDRUM over; 'about' joins O and US loosely.
explanation.definitionFit: Murderous heat or traffic is extremely unpleasant, dreadful to endure.

clue.text: Without waiting? That's showing no concern for others

explanation.surface: A question about the lack of staff, then a comment on selfishness.
explanation.definitionFit: A restaurant where diners help themselves has no table staff; a person acting only for their own advantage is selfish.

clue.text: Foreign money is collected for saint …

parts.note: the franc was the currency of France, Belgium and Switzerland
taken as written

explanation.surface: Money from abroad is gathered in a church collection for a saint's day.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots join this clue to 9 across, which carries on the money theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Francis of Assisi is a famous holy man canonised by the Church.

clue.text: Youngsters are too hot

explanation.surface: Children are overheating.
explanation.definitionFit: Fry are young fish; people baking in the sun are said to fry.

clue.text: Allow notice in front of US university

indicators.note: in front of means the notice comes ahead of the university in the answer

parts.note: an ad is a notice, an advertisement
MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: Permission is posted on a board outside an American college.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit someone is to let them in, to permit entry.

clue.text: Shavian drama performed in miraculous scene

indicators.note: in means the word for performed goes inside the place name

parts.note: Cana is where Jesus turned water into wine
did means performed

explanation.surface: A play by Shaw is staged in a scene of wonders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shavian' means by George Bernard Shaw.
explanation.definitionFit: Candida is one of Shaw's plays, from 1894.

clue.text: Thus artist initially takes yearly fellowship

parts.note: so means thus
Salvador Dalí was a Spanish surrealist painter

indicators.note: initially means the first letters of the two words after it are taken

explanation.surface: In this way a painter, at the start, joins an annual society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes T and Y from TAKES and YEARLY.
explanation.definitionFit: A sodality is a fraternity or brotherhood, especially a Catholic lay society.

clue.text: … and a little more before meeting at headquarters

indicators.note: before means the coin comes ahead of the meeting in the answer

parts.note: following on from the foreign money of 5 across, a little more money is a cent, a small coin
a rally is a mass meeting

explanation.surface: Continuing the collection: a bit more cash is gathered before a gathering at head office.
explanation.walkthrough: The leading dots link to 5 across, so 'a little more' means a little more money: a CENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done at headquarters happens in the central office, at the heart of an organisation.

clue.text: Unearthed tough material? Just the reverse

indicators.note: the clue says the opposite is true: the material word read backwards gives the answer

parts.note: denim is a hard-wearing cotton cloth used for jeans

explanation.surface: Was some hard-wearing stuff dug up? No, quite the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just the reverse' tells you to write DENIM backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Mined ore has been dug out of the ground, brought up from below the surface.

clue.text: European city, for example, appearing in fiction

indicators.note: appearing in means the example abbreviation sits inside the word for fiction

parts.note: a lie is a fiction, an untruth

explanation.surface: A continental city turns up as an example in a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fiction' looks like novels but means a falsehood.
explanation.definitionFit: Liège is a large Belgian city on the river Meuse.

clue.text: Distortion of law, this, or political stunt

indicators.note: a distortion twists things out of shape, so these three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Bending the law, or a piece of political theatre: which is this?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Distortion of' rearranges LAW, THIS and OR.
explanation.definitionFit: A staged public trial with a predetermined verdict is a propaganda stunt by a regime.

clue.text: It's obvious what a speaker's lips do

explanation.surface: Plainly, a talker's mouth moves.
explanation.definitionFit: An open-and-shut case is clear-cut; lips part and close as someone talks.

clue.text: Dye material worker got for standard-bearer

parts.note: a dye is a colouring agent, colour
serge is a hard-wearing woollen cloth
the worker ant is the crossword's stock worker

explanation.surface: A dyed-cloth worker gets swapped in to carry the flag.
explanation.walkthrough: A COLOUR SERGEANT is a senior army NCO rank, originally the one who guarded the regiment's colours.
explanation.definitionFit: The rank traditionally escorted the regimental flag, so its holder is a carrier of the colours.

clue.text: Check-physical punishment

explanation.surface: An inspection, or a beating.
explanation.definitionFit: A going-over is a thorough examination, and also a beating.

clue.text: Unromantic headmistress said to let opportunity slip

indicators.note: said means the words are spoken and a near-match is heard

parts.note: to let an opportunity slip is to miss the bus

explanation.surface: A loveless head teacher is quoted letting her chance go by.
explanation.walkthrough: Frances Buss was a Victorian headmistress, mocked in the rhyme 'Miss Buss and Miss Beale, Cupid's darts do not feel'.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhyme cast Frances Buss as immune to love, a famously single schoolmistress.

clue.text: Special agent is on visit to make enquiries

indicators.note: special in the sense of specially arranged, so these words are reworked

explanation.surface: A secret agent goes on a visit to ask questions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Special agent' reads as one phrase, but 'Special' is the anagram signal for AGENT IS ON VISIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Investigations are formal inquiries made into a matter.

clue.text: TV broadcast with brain that's pulsating

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are spread and rearranged

explanation.surface: Television with an intelligent edge is lively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges TV and BRAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Vibrant means throbbing with life and energy.

clue.text: Offensive public talk about an honour

indicators.note: about means the talk word wraps around the honour

parts.note: noise is public talk or rumour
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A gossip goes round about someone's award, causing offence.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisome means unpleasant, especially foul-smelling.

clue.text: A very loud boy producing disturbance

parts.note: ff is fortissimo, the musical mark for very loud
Ray is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A noisy lad causes trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: An affray is a public brawl, a breach of the peace.

clue.text: Footwear, very old and damaged

parts.note: a sabot is a wooden clog
aged means very old

explanation.surface: A list of worn shoes: ancient and battered.
explanation.walkthrough: The word sabotage comes from the sabot, a clog workers were said to throw into machinery.
explanation.definitionFit: Sabotaged machinery has been deliberately wrecked.

clue.text: One of those taught in institute? Evidently

indicators.note: in means the letters lie inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Is a pupil found at a school? Clearly.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'insTITUTE Evidently'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutee is a pupil who receives tuition from a tutor.

clue.text: Keen to show this

parts.note: keen here is the verb meaning to wail in mourning, so the clue asks what such wailing displays

explanation.surface: An eager person wants to display something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keen' looks like eager, but it is the Irish verb to lament over the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Keening is a mournful cry, an outward display of sorrow at a death.

clue.text: Not fit, girl needs physical training

parts.note: Una is a girl's name

explanation.surface: An unfit girl needs to do some exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: Unapt means unsuitable, not appropriate for the purpose.

clue.text: Bishop and I have changed our ways

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: changed means the letters of the two words before it are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A bishop confesses that he and the speaker have mended their ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' rearranges I HAVE to make EHAVI.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's ways are their conduct, how they habitually act.

clue.text: Section of plane tree

explanation.surface: A part of a plane tree.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft's bomb bay is a compartment; the bay is a laurel.

clue.text: French composer they disheartened, in jaded state

parts.note: Erik Satie was a French composer

indicators.note: disheartened means the word they loses its heart, leaving its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A French composer's crowd lost heart and grew weary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' takes the middle out of THEY, leaving TY.
explanation.definitionFit: Satiety is the state of having had more than enough, so one is weary of it.

clue.text: Restyle in a way that's avoiding unnecessary detail

indicators.note: in a way here means in some fashion, so the word restyle is rearranged

explanation.surface: Rework your prose so that it cuts out padding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a way' rearranges RESTYLE; the definition describes a manner of speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking briefly, without padding, is speaking concisely.
